claim: Complex macro-scale patterns of brain activity that emerge during periods of wakeful rest provide insight into the organisation of neural function.
source: Complex macro-scale patterns of brain activity that emerge during periods of wakeful rest provide insight into the organisation of neural function, how these differentiate individuals based on their traits, and the neural basis of different types of self-generated thoughts.
evidence: This is a general statement about the value of resting-state brain activity research, drawing on established scientific consensus in the field.

claim: Brain activity during wakeful rest differentiates individuals based on their traits.
source: Complex macro-scale patterns of brain activity that emerge during periods of wakeful rest provide insight into the organisation of neural function, how these differentiate individuals based on their traits, and the neural basis of different types of self-generated thoughts.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge in the field about individual differences in resting-state brain activity.

claim: Brain activity during wakeful rest provides insight into the neural basis of different types of self-generated thoughts.
source: Complex macro-scale patterns of brain activity that emerge during periods of wakeful rest provide insight into the organisation of neural function, how these differentiate individuals based on their traits, and the neural basis of different types of self-generated thoughts.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research in the field.

claim: The unconstrained nature of brain activity at rest makes it difficult to disentangle neural features related to personality traits from those related to thoughts occurring at rest.
source: Although brain activity during wakeful rest is valuable for understanding important features of human cognition, its unconstrained nature makes it difficult to disentangle neural features related to personality traits from those related to the thoughts occurring at rest.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the methodological challenges in studying resting-state brain activity.

claim: Recent work on ongoing conscious thought highlights interactions between three brain networks: ventral attention network, dorsal attention network, and default mode network.
source: Our study builds on recent perspectives from work on ongoing conscious thought that highlight the interactions between three brain networks – ventral and dorsal attention networks, as well as the default mode network.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent theoretical work in the field.

claim: For more introverted individuals, regions of the ventral attention network were functionally more aligned to regions of the somatomotor system and the default mode network.
source: Our analysis established that for more introverted individuals, regions of the ventral attention network were functionally more aligned to regions of the somatomotor system and the default mode network.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's data analysis, as shown in the results section and Figure 4.

claim: A pattern of detailed self-generated thought was associated with a decoupling of regions of dorsal attention from regions in the default mode network.
source: At the same time, a pattern of detailed self-generated thought was associated with a decoupling of regions of dorsal attention from regions in the default mode network.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's data analysis, as shown in the results section and Figure 5.

claim: Interactions between attention systems and the default mode network are important influences on ongoing thought at rest.
source: Our study, therefore, establishes that interactions between attention systems and the default mode network are important influences on ongoing thought at rest and highlights the value of integrating contemporary perspectives on conscious experience when understanding patterns of brain activity at rest.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings, integrating the data with theoretical perspectives.

claim: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest have the potential for elucidating different types of psychiatric conditions.
source: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest have the potential for elucidating the organisation of neural function, different types of psychiatric conditions (Cao et al., 2018; Koban et al., 2021), developmental changes including those during adolescence and old age (Dosenbach et al., 2010; Cui et al., 2020; Gratton et al., 2020; Wen et al., 2020), neurological disorders (Zhang et al., 2021) and are important for revealing the neural basis behind the landscape of self-generated experiences (Karapanagiotidis et al., 2019; Mckeown et al., 2020; Kucyi et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest have the potential for elucidating developmental changes including those during adolescence and old age.
source: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest have the potential for elucidating the organisation of neural function, different types of psychiatric conditions (Cao et al., 2018; Koban et al., 2021), developmental changes including those during adolescence and old age (Dosenbach et al., 2010; Cui et al., 2020; Gratton et al., 2020; Wen et al., 2020), neurological disorders (Zhang et al., 2021) and are important for revealing the neural basis behind the landscape of self-generated experiences (Karapanagiotidis et al., 2019; Mckeown et al., 2020; Kucyi et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest have the potential for elucidating neurological disorders.
source: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest have the potential for elucidating the organisation of neural function, different types of psychiatric conditions (Cao et al., 2018; Koban et al., 2021), developmental changes including those during adolescence and old age (Dosenbach et al., 2010; Cui et al., 2020; Gratton et al., 2020; Wen et al., 2020), neurological disorders (Zhang et al., 2021) and are important for revealing the neural basis behind the landscape of self-generated experiences (Karapanagiotidis et al., 2019; Mckeown et al., 2020; Kucyi et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest are important for revealing the neural basis behind the landscape of self-generated experiences.
source: Macro-scale patterns of brain activity at rest have the potential for elucidating the organisation of neural function, different types of psychiatric conditions (Cao et al., 2018; Koban et al., 2021), developmental changes including those during adolescence and old age (Dosenbach et al., 2010; Cui et al., 2020; Gratton et al., 2020; Wen et al., 2020), neurological disorders (Zhang et al., 2021) and are important for revealing the neural basis behind the landscape of self-generated experiences (Karapanagiotidis et al., 2019; Mckeown et al., 2020; Kucyi et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Interpreting neural activity recorded during resting-state functional MRI is challenging compared to controlled experimental conditions.
source: However, compared to controlled experimental conditions, interpreting neural activity recorded during resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) is challenging, partly because both trait-level aspects of the individual and the inherently complex and dynamic nature of ongoing experience at rest are both contributory factors to the observed brain activity (Smallwood et al., 2021b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and reflects established knowledge about methodological challenges.

claim: Both trait-level aspects of the individual and the inherently complex and dynamic nature of ongoing experience at rest are contributory factors to observed brain activity during resting-state fMRI.
source: However, compared to controlled experimental conditions, interpreting neural activity recorded during resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) is challenging, partly because both trait-level aspects of the individual and the inherently complex and dynamic nature of ongoing experience at rest are both contributory factors to the observed brain activity (Smallwood et al., 2021b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The meaning of different patterns of neural activity can be usefully constrained by pairing imaging data at rest with additional measures.
source: It has recently been suggested that the meaning of different patterns of neural activity can be usefully constrained by pairing imaging data at rest with additional measures (Finn, 2021), for example, by accounting for the patterns of thoughts individuals experience at rest (Karapanagiotidis et al., 2020; Karapanagiotidis et al., 2021; Mckeown et al., 2020; Gonzalez-Castillo et al., 2021; Kucyi et al., 2021), trait variation in how people think during tasks (Smallwood et al., 2016), or features of their personality (Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The ventral attention network helps gate access to conscious experience regardless of the focus of attention.
source: From this perspective, key hubs of the VAN, such as the anterior insula and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, help gate access to conscious experience regardless of the focus of attention.
evidence: This is a theoretical claim based on the tri-partite network account discussed in the introduction.

claim: The ventral attention network influences interactions between the dorsal attention network and the default mode network.
source: This is hypothesised to occur because the VAN influences interactions between the DAN, which is more important for external mental content (Corbetta and Shulman, 2002), and the DMN, which is important when states (including tasks) rely more on internal representations (Smallwood et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is a theoretical claim supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The dorsal attention network is more important for external mental content.
source: This is hypothesised to occur because the VAN influences interactions between the DAN, which is more important for external mental content (Corbetta and Shulman, 2002), and the DMN, which is important when states (including tasks) rely more on internal representations (Smallwood et al., 2021a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The default mode network is important when states (including tasks) rely more on internal representations.
source: This is hypothesised to occur because the VAN influences interactions between the DAN, which is more important for external mental content (Corbetta and Shulman, 2002), and the DMN, which is important when states (including tasks) rely more on internal representations (Smallwood et al., 2021a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Activity levels in the anterior insula determine whether stimuli presented at perceptual threshold are consciously perceived.
source: For example, Huang et al., 2021 established that activity levels in the anterior insula determine whether stimuli presented at perceptual threshold are consciously perceived, and this gating of external input emerged as a consequence of changes in the normal interactions between the DAN and DMN.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Gating of external input by the anterior insula emerges as a consequence of changes in the normal interactions between the dorsal attention network and default mode network.
source: For example, Huang et al., 2021 established that activity levels in the anterior insula determine whether stimuli presented at perceptual threshold are consciously perceived, and this gating of external input emerged as a consequence of changes in the normal interactions between the DAN and DMN.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Disruptions to activity in the insula through anaesthesia result in reductions in self-generated mental imagery.
source: They also found that disruptions to activity in the insula through anaesthesia resulted in reductions in self-generated mental imagery.
evidence: This statement refers to findings from Huang et al., 2021, as indicated by the context.

claim: Activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is correlated with self-generated episodic thoughts during periods of low demands.
source: For example, they found activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (a member of the VAN according to a parcellation by Yeo et al., 2011) was correlated with apparently contradictory patterns of ongoing thought: (i) self-generated episodic thoughts during periods of low demands, and (ii) patterns of detailed task focus when individuals were engaged in demanding external task.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Turnbull et al., 2019a.

claim: Activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is correlated with patterns of detailed task focus when individuals are engaged in demanding external tasks.
source: For example, they found activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (a member of the VAN according to a parcellation by Yeo et al., 2011) was correlated with apparently contradictory patterns of ongoing thought: (i) self-generated episodic thoughts during periods of low demands, and (ii) patterns of detailed task focus when individuals were engaged in demanding external task.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Turnbull et al., 2019a.

claim: Neural activity within regions of the dorsal parietal cortex within the dorsal attention network is exclusively reduced when participants engage in self-generated thinking.
source: In the same study, however, neural activity within regions of the dorsal parietal cortex within the DAN was exclusively reduced when participants engaged in self-generated thinking, highlighting a parallel neglect of external input seen by Huang and colleagues.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Turnbull et al., 2019a.

claim: Trait variance in the ability to focus on self-generated experience in laboratory situations with lower task demands is associated with decoupling of signals arising from the dorsal attention network and default mode network at rest.
source: Finally, in a second study, Turnbull and colleagues found that at rest trait variance in the ability to focus on self-generated experience in laboratory situations with lower task demands is associated with decoupling of signals arising from the DAN and DMN (Turnbull et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Turnbull et al., 2019b.

claim: Regions of the ventral attention network may be important for gating conscious access to different types of content by biasing interactions between the dorsal attention network and default mode network.
source: Summarising this emerging evidence, studies focused on understanding ongoing thought patterns from different perspectives converge on the view that regions of the VAN may be important for gating conscious access to different types of content by biasing interactions between the DAN and DMN (Huang et al., 2021; Smallwood et al., 2021b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and represents a synthesis of evidence.

claim: The study sample included 144 participants.
source: Our sample was a cohort of 144 participants who underwent a 1-hr resting-state scan.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's sample size.

claim: Participants underwent a 1-hour resting-state scan.
source: Our sample was a cohort of 144 participants who underwent a 1-hr resting-state scan.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: Participants were interrupted on four occasions during the 1-hour scan to answer questions about their experiences at rest using multidimensional experience sampling.
source: Across this 1-hr period, participants were interrupted on four occasions to answer a set of questions about their experiences at rest using multidimensional experience sampling (MDES), similar to a number of prior neuroimaging studies (Smallwood et al., 2016; Poerio et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: Participants completed a battery of measures assessing features of their personality during a different session.
source: During a different session, the same participants also completed a battery of measures assessing features of their personality (such as the Big Five; Costa and McCrae, 2008) as well as subclinical/psychiatric traits such as trait anxiety and depression (Zigmond and Snaith, 1983).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: The study used the BrainSpace toolbox to provide whole-brain low-dimensional representations of functional brain organisation.
source: Since our research question depends on understanding the hypothesised relationship between large-scale networks (VAN, DMN, and DAN), we used the BrainSpace toolbox (Vos de Wael et al., 2020) to provide whole-brain low-dimensional representations of functional brain organisation, generating maps which represent the similarities and differences in the activity within different systems.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: The study used principal component analysis to produce low-dimensional representations of both traits and thoughts.
source: We used R version 4.2.0 (R Development Core Team, 2021) to produce low-dimensional representations of both traits and thoughts using principal component analysis (PCA).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: The study performed multiple regression to identify how brain network organisation varies with traits and states.
source: Using these two sets of data, we performed multiple regression to identify how brain network organisation varies with traits and states.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: The dataset used is part of the MPI-Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body database.
source: The dataset used here is part of the MPI-Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body database (Mendes et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data source.

claim: The complete dataset consists of a battery of self-reported personality measures, measures of spontaneous thought, task data, and structural and resting-state functional MRI from participants between 20 and 75 years of age.
source: The complete dataset consists of a battery of self-reported personality measures, measures of spontaneous thought, task data, and structural and resting-state functional MRI from participants between 20 and 75 years of age.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the dataset characteristics.

claim: Data were collected over a period of 5 days, with the MRI sessions always falling on day 3.
source: Data were collected over a period of 5 days, with the MRI sessions always falling on day 3.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data collection protocol.

claim: The study limited investigation to participants under 50 years of age who had complete data from at least three resting-state scans.
source: We limited our investigation to personality and thought self-reports, and rs-fMRI from participants under 50 years of age, who had complete data from at least three resting-state scans.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's inclusion criteria.

claim: The resulting sample included 144 participants (74 men, mean age = 26.77 years, SD = 4.03; 70 women, mean age = 26.93 years, SD = 5.55).
source: The resulting sample included 144 participants (74 men, mean age = 26.77 years, SD = 4.03; 70 women, mean age = 26.93 years, SD = 5.55).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's sample characteristics.

claim: The current sample includes 1 hour of fully pre-processed resting-state fMRI data from 144 participants.
source: The current sample includes 1 hr of fully pre-processed rs-fMRI data from 144 participants (four scans from 135 participants, and three scans from 9 participants whose data were missing or incomplete).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data included in the study.

claim: Four scans were obtained from 135 participants, and three scans from 9 participants whose data were missing or incomplete.
source: The current sample includes 1 hr of fully pre-processed rs-fMRI data from 144 participants (four scans from 135 participants, and three scans from 9 participants whose data were missing or incomplete).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data completeness.

claim: The resting-state fMRI was performed in four adjacent 15-minute sessions each immediately followed by multidimensional experience sampling.
source: The rs-fMRI was performed in four adjacent 15 mi sessions each immediately followed by MDES which retrospectively measured various dimensions of spontaneous thought during the scan.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: Images were acquired in axial orientation using T2∗-weighted gradient-echo echo planar imaging sensitive to blood oxygen level-dependent contrast.
source: Images were acquired in axial orientation using T2∗-weighted gradient-echo echo planar imaging sensitive to blood oxygen level-dependent contrast.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the imaging acquisition parameters.

claim: The multidimensional experience sampling battery included 12 statements which participants rated on a visual analogue scale with 5% response increments from 0% to 100%.
source: The MDES battery included 12 statements (Table 1) which participants rated on a visual analogue scale with 5% response increments that go from 0% = "describes my thoughts not at all" to 100% = "describes my thoughts completely".
evidence: This is a direct statement about the measurement methodology.

claim: The study included data from 21 personality questionnaires.
source: To provide a broad description of individual traits, we included data from the following 21 questionnaires (Table 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the measures included in the study.

claim: Principal component analysis was performed on 71 trait variables from 21 questionnaires of 144 participants.
source: Seventy-one scores from the personality questionnaires of 144 participants were included and missing data (3.15% of including all variables) were imputed by the variable mean. PCA was performed on this matrix and five 'trait' components (henceforth referred to as 'traits') were selected on the basis of eigenvalues >1, using the Kaiser–Guttman criterion (Joliffe, 2002) and their congruence with the previously well-established 'Big Five' personality traits (Digman, 1990; Cobb-Clark and Schurer, 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: Missing data (3.15% of all variables) were imputed by the variable mean.
source: Seventy-one scores from the personality questionnaires of 144 participants were included and missing data (3.15% of including all variables) were imputed by the variable mean.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data preprocessing.

claim: Five trait components were selected on the basis of eigenvalues >1, using the Kaiser–Guttman criterion.
source: PCA was performed on this matrix and five 'trait' components (henceforth referred to as 'traits') were selected on the basis of eigenvalues >1, using the Kaiser–Guttman criterion (Joliffe, 2002) and their congruence with the previously well-established 'Big Five' personality traits (Digman, 1990; Cobb-Clark and Schurer, 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the component selection methodology.

claim: The five trait components largely map onto the 'Big Five' personality factors: neuroticism, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and openness to experience.
source: The five trait components, independent of the direction of loadings, largely map onto the 'Big Five' personality factors: neuroticism, conscientiousness (positive loading on 'procrastination' in our PCA result), extraversion (positive loading on 'introversion' in our PCA result), agreeableness (positive loading on anti-social in our results), and openness to experience, respectively.
evidence: This is a finding from the PCA analysis, as shown in Figure 1A.

claim: For the multidimensional experience sampling data, separate instances of responding for each participant were concatenated, resulting in a matrix with 576 observations of 12 variables.
source: For the MDES data, separate instances of responding for each participant were concatenated, resulting in a matrix with 576 observations of 12 variables.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data processing methodology.

claim: Principal component analysis of the multidimensional experience sampling data revealed five thought patterns with eigenvalues >1, explaining 65.4% of the variance.
source: Application of PCA to the MDES questions revealed five 'thought patterns' (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) with eigenvalues >1, explaining 65.4% of the variance.
evidence: This is a finding from the PCA analysis, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The five thought patterns were named 'modality' (image vs words), 'positive episodic social', 'specific internal', 'self-relevant', and 'prospective'.
source: Based on the most heavily loaded dimensions within each pattern, we named these 'modality' (image vs words), 'positive episodic social', 'specific internal', 'self-relevant', and 'prospective'.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the naming of the thought patterns based on the PCA results.

claim: Varimax rotation was applied to both trait and thought component solutions to optimise the distinctiveness of each component.
source: Varimax rotation was applied to both solutions to optimise the distinctiveness of each component.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: The five thought pattern scores were averaged across the four scans, resulting in one score for each thought pattern for each participant.
source: The five thought pattern scores were then averaged across the four scans, resulting in one score for each thought pattern for each participant, describing their location on a particular thought dimension.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data processing methodology.

claim: Functional time series for each participant was extracted using the Schaefer 400 parcellation.
source: Functional time series for each participant was extracted using the Schaefer 400 parcellation (Schaefer et al., 2018) using the fully pre-processed data from all four resting-state scans.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data processing methodology.

claim: A 400 × 400 connectivity matrix was calculated from the time series for each participant using Pearson correlation.
source: The data from separate scans were concatenated, and a 400 × 400 connectivity matrix was calculated from the resulting time series for each participant using Pearson correlation.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: A group connectivity matrix of the whole sample was calculated by averaging the 144 individual matrices.
source: A group connectivity matrix of the whole sample was calculated by averaging the 144 individual matrices.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: Ten macro-scale gradients were calculated for the group.
source: In order to summarise whole-brain connectivity in a low-dimensional space, we performed gradient analysis using the BrainSpace toolbox (Vos de Wael et al., 2020). Ten macro-scale gradients were calculated for the group (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: PCA was chosen for gradient calculation because it provides better reliability and higher phenotypic predictive value for connectivity gradients compared to nonlinear decomposition methods.
source: We chose the PCA approach for gradient calculation, as Hong et al., 2020 have shown that compared to nonlinear decomposition methods, PCA provides better reliability and higher phenotypic predictive value for connectivity gradients.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hong et al., 2020.

claim: Group gradients were aligned to a subsample of the HCP dataset included in BrainSpace.
source: For ease of interpretation and comparability, group gradients were aligned to a subsample of the HCP dataset (Van Essen et al., 2013) included in BrainSpace.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: Individual gradients were calculated for each participant and aligned to the group-level gradients, resulting in a 400 × 10 matrix for each participant.
source: Individual gradients were calculated for each participant, aligned to the group-level gradients, resulting in a 400 × 10 matrix for each participant.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: Subsequent regression analyses were limited to the first three group-aligned gradients.
source: Subsequent regression analyses were limited to the first three group-aligned gradients, which have been relatively well characterised in previous work (Margulies et al., 2016; Mckeown et al., 2020; Turnbull et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: Neurosynth decoding was performed on the group gradient maps to visualise the functional axis captured by each gradient.
source: To visualise the functional axis captured by each gradient, we performed Neurosynth (Yarkoni et al., 2011) decoding on the group gradient maps (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: The average gradient score was calculated for all parcels within each of the seven connectivity networks described by Yeo and colleagues.
source: Further, we calculated the average gradient score for all parcels within each of the seven connectivity networks described by Yeo and colleagues (Yeo et al., 2011; Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: Intra-class correlation coefficients were calculated for the thought patterns to quantify their stability over the whole scanning period.
source: To quantify the stability of thoughts and connectivity gradients over the whole scanning period, intra-class correlation coefficients (ICCs) were calculated for the thought patterns and following Hong et al., 2020, discriminability indices (Bridgeford et al., 2021) were calculated for whole gradients by treating the four scans and subsequent thought probes as separate instances.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: Discriminability indices were calculated for whole gradients to quantify their stability over the whole scanning period.
source: To quantify the stability of thoughts and connectivity gradients over the whole scanning period, intra-class correlation coefficients (ICCs) were calculated for the thought patterns and following Hong et al., 2020, discriminability indices (Bridgeford et al., 2021) were calculated for whole gradients by treating the four scans and subsequent thought probes as separate instances.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data analysis methodology.

claim: The two-way mixed-effects model (type 3 ICC) was used for quantifying test–retest reliability.
source: We used the two-way mixed-effects model (i.e. type 3 ICC) used for quantifying test–retest reliability where samples cannot be considered independent (Koo and Li, 2016).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: Only the 135 participants who had four full-length resting-state scans were included in the stability analysis.
source: Only the 135 participants who had four full-length resting-state scans were included in this analysis.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the inclusion criteria for the stability analysis.

claim: Multiple multivariate regression was used to investigate the relationship between individual differences in traits, thoughts, and macro-scale cortical gradients.
source: To investigate the relationship between individual differences in traits, thoughts, and macro-scale cortical gradients, we used multiple multivariate regression as implemented in the MATLAB SurfStat Toolbox (Worsley et al., 2009; http://www.math.mcgill.ca/keith/surfstat/).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: 400 separate linear models were estimated for 400 parcels, with the gradient scores from the first three gradients as the dependent variables.
source: In total, 400 separate linear models were estimated for 400 parcels, with the gradient scores from the first three gradients as the dependent variables, and with five trait scores (Figure 1A) and five thought scores (Figure 1B), as well as nuisance variables age, motion, and gender included as independent variables.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: Five trait scores, five thought scores, and nuisance variables (age, motion, and gender) were included as independent variables in the regression models.
source: In total, 400 separate linear models were estimated for 400 parcels, with the gradient scores from the first three gradients as the dependent variables, and with five trait scores (Figure 1A) and five thought scores (Figure 1B), as well as nuisance variables age, motion, and gender included as independent variables.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: Significant effects from 400 parcels were corrected for false discovery rate (q < 0.05) at the multivariate (three gradients) level.
source: The resulting significant effects from 400 parcels were corrected for false discovery rate (q < 0.05) (Storey, 2003) at the multivariate (three gradients) level.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: Follow-up univariate analyses were performed on the resulting parcels for each gradient separately, and effects were further Bonferroni-corrected (pbonf<0.025).
source: In order to test which gradient score was affected, follow-up univariate analyses were performed on the resulting parcels for each gradient separately, and effects were further Bonferroni-corrected (pbonf<0.025) for the total number of comparisons performed for all parcels (including the analyses of all three gradients) for each variable.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: Multiple multivariate regression was performed with thoughts as dependent variables and traits as independent variables to examine how trait components related to thought components.
source: Additionally, to see how the trait components related to the thought components, we performed multiple multivariate regression with the thoughts as dependent variables and traits as independent variables.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: The five trait components explained 48.4% of the variance in the personality questionnaire data.
source: Application of PCA to the battery of personality questionnaires resulted in five 'traits' (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1) with eigenvalues >1, explaining 48.4% of the variance.
evidence: This is a finding from the PCA analysis.

claim: The five thought patterns showed low-to-moderate agreement between individual scores from single sessions.
source: The five thought patterns showed low-to-moderate agreement between individual scores from single sessions (modality = 0.5856, positive episodic-social = 0.4531, specific internal = 0.5226, self-relevant = 0.5832, prospective = 0.3118), indicating a degree of variability between sessions.
evidence: This is a finding from the ICC analysis.

claim: The average of all thought pattern scores across sessions had high intra-class correlation coefficients for the first four components.
source: The average of all scores had high ICCs for the first four components (modality = 0.8497, positive episodic social = 0.7783, specific internal = 0.8141, self-relevant = 0.8484, prospective = 0.6444).
evidence: This is a finding from the ICC analysis.

claim: A high score on trait neuroticism was significantly associated with less 'positive episodic social' thought (ß = –0.229, 95% CI = [-0.389 –0.07], p=0.005, partial η² = 0.055).
source: Univariate follow-up showed that a high score on trait neuroticism was significantly associated with less 'positive episodic social' thought (pattern 2; ß = –0.229, 95% CI = [-0.389 –0.07], p=0.005, partial η² = 0.055) as well as greater 'self-relevant' thought (pattern 4; ß = 0.229, 95% CI = [0.066 0.391], p=0.006, partial η² = 0.053) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis.

claim: A high score on trait neuroticism was significantly associated with greater 'self-relevant' thought (ß = 0.229, 95% CI = [0.066 0.391], p=0.006, partial η² = 0.053).
source: Univariate follow-up showed that a high score on trait neuroticism was significantly associated with less 'positive episodic social' thought (pattern 2; ß = –0.229, 95% CI = [-0.389 –0.07], p=0.005, partial η² = 0.055) as well as greater 'self-relevant' thought (pattern 4; ß = 0.229, 95% CI = [0.066 0.391], p=0.006, partial η² = 0.053) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis.

claim: The first gradient (G1) differentiates between visual regions at one end and default mode network at the other.
source: The first gradient (G1) differentiates between visual regions at one end and DMN at the other.
evidence: This is a finding from the gradient analysis, as shown in Figure 2.

claim: The second gradient (G2) describes the dissociation between somatomotor and visual cortices.
source: The second gradient (G2) describes the dissociation between somatomotor and visual cortices.
evidence: This is a finding from the gradient analysis, as shown in Figure 2.

claim: The third gradient (G3) captures the segregation between different transmodal systems (the default mode network vs the fronto-parietal system).
source: The third gradient (G3) captures the segregation between different transmodal systems (the DMN vs the fronto-parietal system).
evidence: This is a finding from the gradient analysis, as shown in Figure 2.

claim: The three gradients are largely similar to those reported by Margulies et al., 2016 and subsequent literature.

evidence: This statement compares the current findings to prior research, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Single gradients tended to be stable over the four sessions, with a discriminability index of 0.964 for gradient 1, 0.918 for gradient 2, and 0.983 for gradient 3.
source: Single gradients tended to be stable over the four sessions, with a discriminability index of 0.964 for gradient 1, 0.918 for gradient 2, and 0.983 for gradient 3 over four adjacent scans from 135 participants.

claim: Discriminability indices are similar to those previously reported by Hong et al., 2020.
source: Discriminability indices are similar to those previously reported by Hong et al., 2020.

claim: Both trait 'introversion' and a pattern describing 'specific internal' thought showed significant effects at the multivariate level in the regression analysis.
source: In these analyses, both trait 'introversion' and a pattern describing 'specific internal' thought showed significant effects at the multivariate level.
evidence: This is a finding from the multiple multivariate regression analysis.

claim: Along the first gradient, a parcel within the right orbitofrontal cortex (within the executive control network) showed more similarity with transmodal regions for individuals high on introversion.
source: Along the first gradient, a parcel within the right orbitofrontal cortex (within the executive control network, shown in orange) showed more similarity with transmodal regions for individuals high on introversion.
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis, as shown in Figure 4 and Table 3.

claim: Six parcels within the ventral attention network, including anterior insula, operculum, and cingulate cortex, were closer to the somatomotor end along gradient 2 for individuals high on introversion.
source: Six parcels within the VAN, including anterior insula, operculum, and cingulate cortex, were closer to the somatomotor end along gradient 2 (shown in purple).
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis, as shown in Figure 4 and Table 3.

claim: The same ventral attention network regions showed lower scores along the third gradient in participants with higher introversion scores, indicating stronger integration with the default mode network.
source: The same regions showed lower scores along the third gradient in participants with higher introversion scores, indicating stronger integration with the DMN.
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis, as shown in Figure 4 and Table 3.

claim: A parcel within posterior cingulate cortex (control network) was more segregated from the visual end of gradient 2 in participants with higher introversion scores.
source: A parcel within posterior cingulate cortex (control) was also more segregated from the visual end of gradient 2 in participants with higher introversion scores.
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis, as shown in Figure 4 and Table 3.

claim: Relationships with patterns of more specific internal cognition were confined to the dorsal attention and visual networks.
source: Relationships with patterns of more specific internal cognition were confined to the dorsal attention and visual networks.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the univariate follow-up analysis.

claim: A region within the superior parietal lobule (dorsal attention network) had lower scores on the first gradient (more transmodal) and higher scores on the second gradient (less visual) when ongoing experience was more 'specific' and 'internal'.
source: A region within the superior parietal lobule (DAN) had lower scores on the first gradient (more transmodal) and higher scores on the second gradient (less visual), indicating less similarity with visual regions whose ongoing experience was more 'specific' and 'internal'.
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis, as shown in Figure 5 and Table 3.

claim: Along the third gradient, higher 'specific internal' thought scores were associated with greater separation between superior parietal lobule regions and the default mode network.
source: Along the third gradient, higher 'specific internal' thought scores were associated with greater separation between these regions and the DMN.
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis, as shown in Figure 5 and Table 3.

claim: A parcel within the parahippocampal gyrus/extrastriate (visual network) showed a broad spread along gradient one, with participants with higher 'specific internal' thought scores falling on the transmodal/default mode network side and participants with lower scores closer to the visual system side.
source: Finally, a parcel within the parahippocampal gyrus/extrastriate (visual network) showed a broad spread along gradient one, with participants with higher 'specific internal' thought scores falling on the transmodal/DMN side and participants with lower scores (higher 'surroundings') closer to the visual system side.
evidence: This is a finding from the univariate follow-up analysis, as shown in Figure 5 and Table 3.

claim: Individuals who were high on dispositional 'introversion' showed variation in anterior insula, overlying operculum, and anterior cingulate cortex.
source: For example, it has been hypothesised that the VAN helps adjudicate between internal and external influences on ongoing thought (Huang et al., 2021; Smallwood et al., 2021b), and we found that individuals who were high on dispositional 'introversion' showed variation in anterior insula, overlying operculum, and ACC: all regions making up part of the VAN.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the regression analysis.

claim: For more introverted people, ventral attention network regions showed greater alignment with somatomotor regions and less with visual cortex (gradient 2).
source: For more introverted people, these regions showed greater alignment with somatomotor regions and less with visual cortex (gradient 2), and greater alignment with the DMN than the fronto-parietal network (gradient 3).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the regression analysis.

claim: For more introverted people, ventral attention network regions showed greater alignment with the default mode network than the fronto-parietal network (gradient 3).
source: For more introverted people, these regions showed greater alignment with somatomotor regions and less with visual cortex (gradient 2), and greater alignment with the DMN than the fronto-parietal network (gradient 3).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the regression analysis.

claim: Prior studies have found that regions of sensorimotor cortex are linked to deliberate mind-wandering.
source: Notably, prior studies have found that regions of sensorimotor cortex are linked to deliberate mind-wandering (Golchert et al., 2017) and individuals who tend to generate patterns of episodic social cognition during periods of low task demands show greater temporal correlation between the VAN and sensorimotor cortex (Turnbull et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Individuals who tend to generate patterns of episodic social cognition during periods of low task demands show greater temporal correlation between the ventral attention network and sensorimotor cortex.
source: Notably, prior studies have found that regions of sensorimotor cortex are linked to deliberate mind-wandering (Golchert et al., 2017) and individuals who tend to generate patterns of episodic social cognition during periods of low task demands show greater temporal correlation between the VAN and sensorimotor cortex (Turnbull et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Introversion reflects a predisposition towards internal subjective states rather than external objects.
source: Introversion reflects a predisposition towards internal subjective states rather than external objects (Jung, 1995), and so our analysis adds to an emerging literature (Golchert et al., 2017; Turnbull et al., 2019b) that suggests that there may be an important relationship between sensorimotor cortex and the VAN in patterns of internal self-generated thought.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jung, 1995.

claim: There may be an important relationship between sensorimotor cortex and the ventral attention network in patterns of internal self-generated thought.
source: Introversion reflects a predisposition towards internal subjective states rather than external objects (Jung, 1995), and so our analysis adds to an emerging literature (Golchert et al., 2017; Turnbull et al., 2019b) that suggests that there may be an important relationship between sensorimotor cortex and the VAN in patterns of internal self-generated thought.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the study's findings and prior research.

claim: A pattern of detailed thinking during wakeful rest was correlated with stronger decoupling of a region within dorsal parietal cortex from the visual network (as indexed by changes in both gradients 1 and 2).
source: For example, we found a pattern of detailed thinking during wakeful rest that was correlated with stronger decoupling between a region within dorsal parietal cortex from the visual network (as indexed by changes in both gradients 1 and 2), and greater separation from the DMN (gradient 3).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the regression analysis.

claim: A pattern of detailed thinking during wakeful rest was correlated with greater separation of a region within dorsal parietal cortex from the default mode network (gradient 3).
source: For example, we found a pattern of detailed thinking during wakeful rest that was correlated with stronger decoupling between a region within dorsal parietal cortex from the visual network (as indexed by changes in both gradients 1 and 2), and greater separation from the DMN (gradient 3).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the regression analysis.

claim: The region within dorsal parietal cortex showing decoupling overlaps with a region within the dorsal attention network identified by Turnbull et al., 2019a in which brain activity was reduced during self-generated thoughts relative to external task focus.
source: This region overlaps with a region within the DAN identified by Turnbull et al., 2019a in which brain activity was reduced during self-generated thoughts relative to external task focus, suggesting an important role for the DAN in external facing attention.
evidence: This statement compares the current findings to prior research.

claim: The dorsal attention network has an important role in external facing attention.
source: This region overlaps with a region within the DAN identified by Turnbull et al., 2019a in which brain activity was reduced during self-generated thoughts relative to external task focus, suggesting an important role for the DAN in external facing attention.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the study's findings and prior research.

claim: Individuals who engaged in self-generated thought during situations of low external demand at rest showed greater separation between the dorsal attention network and lateral regions of the default mode network in a region of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
source: Furthermore, using a technique known as 'echoes' analysis (see Leech et al., 2012), Turnbull et al., 2019a established that individuals who engaged in self-generated thought during situations of low external demand at rest showed greater separation between the DAN and lateral regions of the DMN in a region of the dLPFC, also a member of the VAN.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Greater segregation between the dorsal attention network and the default mode network is associated with the capacity to engage in thoughts that are less linked to the external environment.
source: Thus, our study confirms prior studies that highlight that greater segregation between the DAN and the DMN in the capacity to engage in thoughts that are less linked to the external environment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings and prior research.

claim: The convergence between the current analysis and perspectives from research on conscious experience highlights a high degree of overlap in both the regions identified and the hypothesised functions.
source: Together, the convergence between the current analysis and perspectives from research on conscious experience highlights a high degree of overlap in both the regions identified and the hypothesised functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the study's findings to prior research.

claim: With appropriate methodology, neural accounts of conscious experience provide an important valuable way to make sense of brain-cognition links observed at rest.
source: Our observations are important, therefore, because they help establish that with the appropriate methodology (Mckeown et al., 2020; Finn, 2021; Gonzalez-Castillo et al., 2021) neural accounts of conscious experience (Huang et al., 2021; Smallwood et al., 2021b) provide an important valuable way to make sense of brain-cognition links observed at rest.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings, supported by citations.

claim: The data provides evidence for the 'decoupling' hypothesis of self-generated experience.
source: Second, our data provides evidence for the 'decoupling' hypothesis of self-generated experience (Smallwood, 2013b).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: The decoupling hypothesis assumes that reduced processing of external input allows an internal train of thought to persist in a more detailed manner.
source: This perspective emerged from observations that cortical processing of external inputs is reduced when individuals focus on internal self-generated thought (Smallwood et al., 2008; Kam et al., 2011; Baird et al., 2014) and assumes that this reduced processing of external input allows an internal train of thought to persist in a more detailed manner (p.524, Smallwood, 2013a; Smallwood, 2013b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cortical processing of external inputs is reduced when individuals focus on internal self-generated thought.
source: This perspective emerged from observations that cortical processing of external inputs is reduced when individuals focus on internal self-generated thought (Smallwood et al., 2008; Kam et al., 2011; Baird et al., 2014) and assumes that this reduced processing of external input allows an internal train of thought to persist in a more detailed manner (p.524, Smallwood, 2013a; Smallwood, 2013b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Both personality traits linked to internal focus ('introversion') and patterns of detail experience that are not directed externally ('specific internal thought') are linked to reductions in the similarity between neural activity in regions linked to attention and cognition, with regions of visual cortex.
source: Our data is consistent with this view since both personality traits linked to internal focus ('introversion') and patterns of detail experience that are not directed externally ('specific internal thought') are linked to reductions in the similarity between neural activity in regions linked to attention and cognition, with regions of visual cortex.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The study provides novel insight into how the macro-scale functional patterns across the cortex support the emergence of detailed patterns of internal experience.
source: In this way, our study provides novel insight into how the macro-scale functional patterns across the cortex support the emergence of detailed patterns of internal experience.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: In the study, there was no external task from which thinking needed to be decoupled from.
source: Critically, in our study there was no external task from which thinking needed to be decoupled from, ruling out accounts of this process as a 'lapse' in the normal upregulation of task-relevant material needed for task completion (for discussion, see Franklin et al., 2013; Smallwood, 2013a; Smallwood, 2013b).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study design.

claim: Contemporary work on ongoing conscious thought highlights time and context as key variables necessary for understanding the neural correlates of different features of thinking.
source: For example, contemporary work on ongoing conscious thought highlights time and context as key variables necessary for understanding the neural correlates of different features of thinking (Smallwood et al., 2021b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Under different task conditions, neural correlates between thinking, personality, and neural activity may be different.
source: Since the aim of our study was to focus on the brain at rest, interpretations of our results should bear in mind that under different task conditions neural correlates between thinking, personality, and neural activity may be different.
evidence: This is a speculation about the generalizability of the findings.

claim: Prior studies have established that posterior elements of the default mode network can become integrated into task-positive systems.
source: For example, prior studies have established that posterior elements of the DMN can become integrated into task-positive systems (Krieger-Redwood et al., 2016; Vatansever et al., 2017) and under demanding task conditions the DMN is linked to patterns of task-focused cognition (Sormaz et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Under demanding task conditions, the default mode network is linked to patterns of task-focused cognition.
source: For example, prior studies have established that posterior elements of the DMN can become integrated into task-positive systems (Krieger-Redwood et al., 2016; Vatansever et al., 2017) and under demanding task conditions the DMN is linked to patterns of task-focused cognition (Sormaz et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The analysis focused on 'static' indices of neural activity rather than dynamic measures.
source: Similarly, our analysis focused on 'static' indices of neural activity rather than dynamic measures.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's methodology.

claim: Prior studies have shown that brain–behaviour correlations can be relatively stable over time.
source: We chose to focus on static indices of neural activity because our prior studies have shown that brain–behaviour correlations can be relatively stable over time (Wang et al., 2020), and as we establish in our study these patterns show reasonable stability across a 1-hr session.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The patterns of brain-behaviour correlations show reasonable stability across a 1-hour session.
source: We chose to focus on static indices of neural activity because our prior studies have shown that brain–behaviour correlations can be relatively stable over time (Wang et al., 2020), and as we establish in our study these patterns show reasonable stability across a 1-hr session.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's stability analysis.

claim: The study's findings relating to the dorsal attention network map closely onto studies that use experience sampling to identify momentary correlations between neural activity and experience.
source: Furthermore, our study, particularly with respect to the findings relating to the DAN, map closely onto studies that use experience sampling to identify momentary correlations between neural activity and experience (Turnbull et al., 2019a).
evidence: This statement compares the current findings to prior research.

claim: There are likely to be important dynamic features of ongoing experience that the analysis of static brain organisation cannot capture.
source: Nonetheless, there are likely to be important dynamic features of ongoing experience that our analysis of static brain organisation cannot capture (Kucyi, 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation about the limitations of the study, supported by a citation.

source: Recent discussions in cognitive neuroscience have highlighted the link between sample size and the reproducibility of brain-wide associations with behavioural phenotypes (Marek et al., 2022; Spisak et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent discussions in the field.

claim: In the current data, neuroticism was the most prominent out of all five traits included in the analysis, accounting for 29% of the total variance explained by them.
source: In the current data, neuroticism was the most prominent out of all five traits included in the analysis, accounting for 29% of the total variance explained by them.

source: It is therefore likely that more extensive and robust correlations between thoughts patterns and other traits, as well as thoughts, traits, and macro-scale connectivity patterns, would emerge with data sets with larger sample sizes.
evidence: This is a speculation about what might be found with larger sample sizes.

claim: In the future, it may be important to consider measures of traits that could have relationships to both neural activity and/or experience at rest.
source: In the future, it may also be important to consider measures of traits that could have relationships to both neural activity and/or experience at rest (e.g. self-consciousness [de Caso et al., 2017] or autistic tendencies [Turnbull et al., 2020a]).
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions, supported by citations.

claim: Mapping momentary changes between ongoing experience and neural activity will likely depend on a data set tailored to this question.
source: It is worth noting that mapping momentary changes between ongoing experience and neural activity will likely depend on a data set tailored to this question, in particular in which (i) experience sampling measures are collected more frequently as well as (ii) methodological advances that allow patterns of activity to be mapped without using temporal correlation.
evidence: This is a speculation about methodological requirements for future research.
